items.title: Overview
items.text: Work with PT Sandbox like a pro

items.title: Highlights
items.text:
• Made by experts for experts
  • Scan multiple files on multiple images in one place
  • User-friendly analysis of sandbox logs
  • Analyze files in the sandbox without leaving your favorite terminal

items.title: Installation
items.text:
pipxpypiNix 
pipx install sandbox-cli

pip install sandbox-cli

nix shell 'github:Security-Experts-Community/sandbox-cli'

We recommend installing the utility using pipx. It allows you to install packages in your isolated environments and not break the global venv.

Next step, the Getting started section.

items.title: Changelog
items.text:
All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

The format is based on Keep a Changelog, and this project adheres to Semantic Versioning.

items.title: Changed
items.text:
• Upgraded to cyclopts>=5.3.3. Help now shows value types (PATH, INT, CHOICE); parse errors exit with code 2 in both text and JSON modes; command failures still exit with code 1. Command names must match exactly: use scan-new and re-scan, not scannew or rescan.
  • Migrated documentation to Zensical with the modern theme; terminal examples use standard code blocks instead of Termynal.

items.title: Added
items.text:
• scan and scan-new take --key several times and spread the files over these sandboxes: a sandbox takes the next file as soon as it has a free slot (max-workers), so faster sandboxes take more files; an unreachable sandbox hands its files to the others
  • key field in the --json output of scans

items.title: Breaking changes
items.text:
Every flag now has one meaning across all commands:

Command Before Now scan, scan-new --crashdumps -c --crashdumps -C re-scan --timeout -t (response waiting time) --wait-timeout -W download --logs -l --logs -L download --sample -s --sample -sa report --suspicious -s --suspicious -su images --all -a --all-keys -ak completion --install -i --install -I rules compile OUT positional or --out --out -o only rules test RULES positional or --rules -r positional RULES_DIR only
  • re-scan accepts all download options of scan-new (-a, -A, -f, -C, -p, -am, -dx, -D), not only --debug
  • rules compile accepts the windows/linux aliases like the scan commands
  • download, email, images and report show --key under "Sandbox Options"; report --key is validated
  • --timeout (analysis duration) and --bootkitmon-duration require at least 10 seconds, as the sandbox does
  • scan uses the same progress display as scan-new

items.title: Added
items.text:
• Native terminal progress indicator (OSC 9;4) for scans, re-scans, downloads and other long operations in Ghostty, WezTerm, Windows Terminal, iTerm2 ≥ 3.6.6, VTE-based terminals, mintty and ConEmu, also inside tmux 3.8+; it turns red when an error occurs
  • Synchronized output (DEC mode 2026) for progress displays, which removes flickering in fast terminals (e.g. Ghostty with an unfocused window)
  • SANDBOX_CLI_TERM_PROGRESS and SANDBOX_CLI_SYNC_OUTPUT environment variables to force these features on/off
  • --unpack-archives / -ua for scan-new: archives go through the full scan, which unpacks them with the passwords from the config and analyzes every extracted file; each extracted file gets its own result folder (<image>/<file>/)
  • --procdump-excludes / -pe option for scan-new: a file with regular expressions of process paths excluded from process dumps (like --fileextractor-excludes)
  • key, ssh.password and docker.token in the config accept { env = "..." } and { command = "..." } besides plain strings
  • --json / -J for scan-new, scan, re-scan, download, email, images and report: results as JSON lines on stdout, messages and progress on stderr
  • [DONE]/[ERROR] line per task for download and email
  • With --json a command-level error is printed as {"status": "error", "reason": "…"} on stdout as well

items.title: Changed
items.text:
• Faster startup: --help, --version and shell completion no longer import the sandbox API client
  • Errors exit with a non-zero status code; a failed task, sandbox or email no longer aborts the others, and the command exits with 1 after the rest finished
  • Mistakes are reported before anything is uploaded: missing hook, exclude and extra files, invalid DLL hooks (with file:line), --outbound-connections values that aren't IP addresses, a missing --rules folder, -l without the [docker] section, re-scan traces without drakvuf-trace/tcpdump.pcap, invalid task ids and links in download, a missing report folder
  • report skips unreadable report.json files with an error instead of aborting
  • Logs are unpacked in parallel processes when several images are scanned with --unpack
  • Unpacking uses constant memory instead of loading whole logs, and moves the original files to raw/ instead of copying them
  • download opens one connection per sandbox and --concurrency limits all downloads together
  • download accepts task links without https://, with a port or query string, and matches the link host to the config host ignoring case and port
  • re-scan extracts sandbox_logs.zip to a temporary directory instead of reading the trace into memory
  • Output is not wrapped when stdout is not a terminal, so task links stay on one line
  • Bumped cyclopts to 4.25.3 (the version in nixos-unstable)
  • Dropped the colorama dependency (rich handles the Windows console itself)
  • Migrated git hooks from pre-commit to prek (prek.toml); mypy runs from the locked environment
  • ruff is the only formatter and import sorter (black and isort removed)

items.title: Fixed
items.text:
• scan-new ran archives as a single file and ignored the passwords from the config; it now warns and suggests --unpack-archives
  • Results of tasks with several files on one image (archives) overwrote each other in download and scans
  • An invalid config file crashed with a traceback instead of an error message
  • Files with the same stem (a.exe, a.dll) or the same name in different folders overwrote each other's results; re-scans of zips with the same name did too
  • re-scan didn't find the trace in a result folder unpacked with --unpack
  • report and browser resolved the key secret (env or command) only to build task links
  • A failed unpack reported the task as both done and failed
  • Running unpack on an already unpacked directory deleted the unpacked logs
  • --amsi and --dex downloaded nothing unless combined with -A, -f, -p or -a
  • A progress row stayed on screen forever after an unexpected error in a scan
  • download --query --count N downloaded more than N tasks and could loop over the first page
  • email wrote headers next to the source file instead of the output directory when given a path
  • Scanning a folder sent its subdirectories to the sandbox as files
  • HTTP errors other than 401 were silently swallowed
  • A DLL hook with no-retval and no strategy crashed with IndexError
  • Shortened file names lost the dot before the extension
  • report started a process pool even for a single report
  • The ssh config option was documented as login instead of username

items.title: Configuration
items.text:
The utility is configured via a toml file.

Note

If no sandbox is specified, the functions related to interacting with the sandbox will be unavailable.

items.title: Location
items.text:
Linux / MacOSWindows 
~/.config/sandbox-cli/config.toml
or
$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/sandbox-cli/config.toml

%APPDATA%\sandbox-cli\config.toml

items.title: passwords
items.text:
There is often a need to scan various password-protected zip archives.

Here you can specify a list of frequently used passwords that the sandbox-cli will send to the sandbox for automatic unpacking.

Default: ["infected", "311138", "password", "12345678", "P@ssw0rd!"]

items.title: sandbox
items.text:
Option Description Default name* Custom token name to be used in the parameters when selecting sandboxes. None key * A token received through the sandbox interface. See how to get it in Getting started. None host * The IP address or domain where the sandbox is located. Example: 10.10.10.10 or sandbox.example.com None max-workers The number of simultaneously running jobs. 8 description Optional description for the sandbox key. None

Note

If you specify a higher number of max-workers, the performance will not increase, the tasks will just hang in the queue.

items.title: ssh
items.text: Option Description Default username The user's login on the server None password The user's password on the server None

items.title: browser
items.text:
Here you can specify custom browser to use for opening the analysis links.

Option Description Default path Path to custom browser None args Args to start the browser with None

Note

Every argument must be in separate string.

items.title: rules-path
items.text:
Base path to the rules directory. When set, --rules can be specified as a relative path.

Default: None

items.title: Secrets
items.text:
key, ssh.password and docker.token accept a plain string or a reference to a secret stored elsewhere:

[[sandbox]]
name = "staging"
host = "sandbox.example.com"
key = { command = "pass show sandbox/staging" }   # stdout of a shell command
# key = { env = "SANDBOX_STAGING_KEY" }           # an environment variable
# key = "plain token"                              # a plain string

A reference is resolved only when a command needs that secret, so --help or commands for other sandboxes don't run the command. The trailing newline of the command output is stripped.

items.title: Environment variables
items.text:
Variable Description DEBUG Show the full traceback on unexpected errors SANDBOX_CLI_TERM_PROGRESS 1/0 — force the native terminal progress indicator (OSC 9;4) on/off. Auto-detected by default SANDBOX_CLI_SYNC_OUTPUT 1/0 — force synchronized output (no flickering) on/off. Enabled for terminals by default

The progress indicator is shown in the tab bar / taskbar of terminals that support it: Ghostty, WezTerm, Windows Terminal, iTerm2 ≥ 3.6.6, VTE-based terminals, mintty and ConEmu. Inside tmux it works with tmux 3.8 or newer when the outer terminal supports it (progressbar in tmux display -p '#{client_termfeatures}'); it is disabled inside screen and zellij.

items.title: Full configuration
items.text:
Config example
# passwords that will be sent to the sandbox for unpacking archives
passwords = ["infected", "311138", "password", "12345678", "P@ssw0rd!"]

# Base path to the rules directory (optional)
# rules-path = "/path/to/rules"

# Use this section only if you don't want to use your default browser
# or it works incorrectly
# [browser]
# path to your browser
# path = "C:\\Program Files\\Mozilla Firefox\\firefox.exe"
# args to run your browser with
# args = ["-new-tab"]

# Specify available sandboxes
# Keep in mind that first sandbox is used by default
# name - short name for the sandbox
# key - token used for the sandbox
# host - host of the sandbox
# max-workers - simultaneously running scans
# description - optional description
# ssh username/password - optional params
[[sandbox]]
name = ""
key = ""
host = ""
max-workers = 8
description = ""
ssh = { username = "", password = "" }

[[sandbox]]
name = ""
key = ""
host = ""
max-workers = 8

items.title: Install sandbox-cli
items.text:
sandbox-cli is available as sandbox-cli on PyPI.

Can be installed with pipx (recommended) or pip:

# with pipx
pipx install sandbox-cli

# with pip
pip install sandbox-cli

Also available as Nix package with configuration customization:

First, add repo to flake inputs:

flake.nix
{
  inputs = {
    sandbox-cli = {
      url = "github:Security-Experts-Community/sandbox-cli";
    };
  };
}

Second, write the config for your home-manager configuration (programs.sandbox-cli.settings is 1-1 mapping of the configuration)

module.nix
{ inputs, lib, pkgs, ... }:
{
  imports = [
    inputs.sandbox-cli.homeManagerModules.default
  ];

  programs.sandbox-cli = {
    enable = true;

    settings = {
      sandbox = [
        {
          name = "sample-key-name";
          key = "sample-key";
          host = "127.0.0.1";
          max-workers = 1;
        }
      ];
    };
  };
}

Alternatively you can install the only sandbox-cli app to your environment and write config by hand:

{
    home.packages = [ inputs.sandbox-cli.packages.${pkgs.system}.sandbox-cli ];
}

Alternatively you can use overlay from inputs.sandbox-cli.overlays.default

items.title: Download files
items.text:
Info

For this option, you need to specify at least one sandbox in the config.

It is often necessary to download some information from the task.

If you don't want to poke all the buttons in the interface, you can simply run one of the following commands:

# Download all available data by task id
$ sandbox-cli download --all b2ece7fa-b3db-4ed5-86c7-2bba4b55f563

# Download only sandbox logs and automatically convert
$ sandbox-cli download --logs --unpack b2ece7fa-b3db-4ed5-86c7-2bba4b55f563

# Or you can just provide a link to the task
$ sandbox-cli download --all https://sandbox.example.com/tasks/b2ece7fa-b3db-4ed5-86c7-2bba4b55f563

# You can also download multiple tasks in one request
$ sandbox-cli download --all b2ece7fa-b3db-4ed5-86c7-2bba4b55f563 https://sandbox.example.com/tasks/c7d567f0-5805-4191-a0f1-e35158dc4e80

# Download only the original sample submitted for analysis
$ sandbox-cli download --sample b2ece7fa-b3db-4ed5-86c7-2bba4b55f563

The structure of the downloads directory:

tree
downloads/
├── b2ece7fa-b3db-4ed5-86c7-2bba4b55f563
│   ├── artifacts/
│   ├── debug/
│   ├── drakvuf-trace.log.zst
│   ├── events-correlated.log.gz
│   ├── events-normalized.log.gz
│   ├── process_dump/
│   ├── tcpdump.pcap
│   └── video.mp4
└── c7d567f0-5805-4191-a0f1-e35158dc4e80
    ├── debug/
    ├── drakvuf-trace.log.zst
    ├── events-correlated.log.gz
    ├── events-normalized.log.gz
    ├── tcpdump.pcap
    └── video.mp4

Tip

If you provide a full link to the sandbox, you do not need to specify the key name for this sandbox.

sandbox-cli download --all https://sandbox-1.example.com/tasks/... https://sandbox-2.example.com/tasks/...

For example, if the keys are named sandbox-1 and sandbox-2. The key sandbox-1 will be used to download the first task, and sandbox-2 for the second.

items.title: Analyze emails
items.text:
Info

For this option, you need to specify at least one sandbox in the config.

To get the email headers, specify the eml file in the parameters.

$ sandbox-cli email file.eml

The files will be downloaded to the downloads directory with the headers suffix.

tree
downloads/
└── file.eml.headers

Usage example

It is useful when it is necessary to decode or extract the headers of an email without the content itself.

items.title: Get Public API token
items.text:
Info

If you do not have direct access to the sandbox interface, it is better to request access through your supervisor.

  • Open the Access Tokens tab in the interface.

  • Click on Create access token and fill in the parameters using the example from the screenshot.

  • Now you can copy this token and save it to a config file.

items.title: Structure
items.text:
After the behavioral analysis, you can download the analysis results which include:

  • events-correlated.log.gz - verdicts. In this case, Trojan.Win32.Generic.a;
  • tcpdump.pcap - a file with network events in pcap format;
  • events-normalized.log.gz - enriched events received from the analysis system;
  • drakvuf-trace.log.zst - raw data from the analysis system;

items.title: How to analyze
items.text:
Just call the conv (or unpack) option and specify the file with the downloaded logs. In this case, sandbox_logs.zip:

$ sandbox-cli conv sandbox_logs.zip

[INFO] Unpacking sandbox_logs.zip

The sandbox-cli unpacks logs into a convenient format, decomposes events by plugins, structures output, etc.

tree
sandbox_logs
├── correlated
│   ├── events-correlated.log
│   ├── events-correlated.log.malware
│   └── events-correlated.log.suspicious.Read.File.Data.DLLHijackMapSystem
├── drakvuf-trace
│   └── drakvuf-trace.log
├── network
│   └── tcpdump.pcap
├── normalized
│   ├── events-normalized.log
│   ├── events-normalized.log.apimon
│   ├── events-normalized.log.cpuidmon
│   └── events-normalized.log.syscall
└── raw
    ├── drakvuf-trace.log.zst
    ├── events-correlated.log.gz
    ├── events-normalized.log.gz
    └── tcpdump.pcap

Note

The output is greatly reduced because a lot of information is collected under Windows

Now you can easily find a suspicious event and analyze it.

event
{
  "object.path": "users\\jamie\\desktop\\malware.dll",
  "process.id": "2828",
  "process.name": "users\\jamie\\desktop\\malware.exe",
  "weight": 10,
  "unixtime": "1741811223.840229",
  "detect.name": "Read.File.Data.DLLHijackMapSystem",
  "detect.type": "suspicious",
  "mitre.tid": "T1574"
}

Tip

You can specify not only one file, but also several in a row if you need to parse several logs.

sandbox-cli conv sandbox_logs.zip sandbox_logs_1.zip sandbox_logs_2.zip

items.title: Help
items.text:
$ sandbox-cli conv --help

Usage: sandbox-cli conv TRACES

Convert sandbox logs into an analysis-friendly format.

╭─ Arguments ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ *  TRACES  The path to the folder with the raw traces or with the            │
│            sandbox-logs.zip [required]                                       │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯

items.title: View report
items.text:
After scanning, you need to quickly understand what the sandbox was able to detect and what was not.

To do this, you can generate a short report in the terminal by transferring the directory where the scan data was saved.

$ sandbox-cli report sandbox/

By default, the report will be printed to the terminal as a table.

A glance at the generated output in md format Sample Image Verdict Static Memory Network malware.elf ubuntu-jammy-x64 Trojan-Downloader.Linux.Generic.n ptesc: crime_linux_ZZ_Diicot__Backdoor__NetworkScannerptesc: crime_linux_ZZ_Diicot__Backdoor__Updaterptesc: tool_linux_ZZ_UPX__RiskToolptesc: tool_linux_ZZ_UPX__Trojan__PatchedUPX ET HUNTING curl User-Agent to Dotted QuadSUSPICIOUS [PTsecurity] GET request in TCPWORM [PTsecurity] Trojan.Worm error message (APT Diicot)

Tip

You can specify multiple folders with reports, they will be combined into one and displayed on the screen.

sandbox-cli report sandbox-1/ sandbox-2/

items.title: Help
items.text:
$ sandbox-cli report --help

Usage: sandbox-cli report [OPTIONS] SRC

Generate short report from sandbox scans.

│         [required]                                                           │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
╭─ Parameters ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ --mode -m         Report output format [choices: cli, md] [default: cli]     │
│ --suspicious -su  Include suspicious detects [default: False]                │
│ --json -J         Print results as JSON lines to stdout; messages and        │
│                   progress go to stderr [default: False]                     │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
╭─ Sandbox Options ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ --key -k  The key to access the sandbox main                                 │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯

items.title: Rescan
items.text:
Info

For this option, you need to specify at least one sandbox in the config.

items.title: Quick start
items.text:
$ sandbox-cli scanner re-scan sandbox_logs.zip

[INFO] Using key: name=test-1 max_workers=8
[DONE] sandbox_logs.zip • https://sandbox.example.com/tasks/56ae494b-fffc-11ef-a24b-72ab1bd29c47

items.title: Download options
items.text: The same download options as in scan-new (-a, -d, -A, -f, -C, -p, -am, -dx, -D). Logs are always downloaded.

items.title: Parameters
items.text: Option Description Default --rules / -r The path to the folder with the rules, a platform alias or an archive with already compiled rules. None --out / -o The path where the analysis results will be saved. ./sandbox --local / -l Compile rules locally using Docker (unix only). False --unpack / -U The downloaded logs will be automatically converted. Learn more in Analyzing logs. False --open-browser / -ob Open the analysis link in the default browser. False --wait-timeout / -W How long to wait for the task result in seconds (increase for large traces). 300

items.title: Sandbox Options
items.text: Option Description Default --key / -k The name of the key for accessing a specific sandbox. first sandbox in the config

items.title: Rescan multiple files
items.text: $ sandbox-cli scanner re-scan sandbox_logs.zip sandbox_logs_1.zip sandbox_logs_2.zip

items.title: Rescan with automatic unpacking
items.text: $ sandbox-cli scanner re-scan -U sandbox_logs.zip sandbox_logs_1.zip sandbox_logs_2.zip

items.title: Rescan and view results
items.text:
$ sandbox-cli scanner re-scan -U sandbox_logs.zip sandbox_logs_1.zip sandbox_logs_2.zip

$ sandbox-cli report sandbox/

items.title: Advanced scan
items.text:
Info

For this option, you need to specify at least one sandbox in the config.

items.title: Quick start
items.text:
# "-t" is the time of behavioral analysis
$ sandbox-cli scanner scan-new -t 120 malware

[INFO] Using key: name=escdev max_workers=8
[DONE] [win10-22H2-x64] • malware • https://sandbox.example.com/tasks/eafc5f87-ffac-11ef-96ad-72ab1bd29c47

Note

At startup, a progress bar will be launched with waiting, but this is not shown here.

items.title: Download options
items.text:
The options allow you to additionally configure which files will be downloaded from the task.

Option Description Default --all / -a Enables all of the following options. False --debug / -d All debug files will be downloaded. False --artifacts / -A All created artifacts (files and process dumps) will be downloaded. Combines -f and -p. False --files / -f All files extracted during the analysis will be downloaded. False --crashdumps / -C A special file that is created during the BSOD. By default, this file is not generated by the sandbox. False --procdumps / -p All process dumps during the analysis will be downloaded. False --amsi / -am AMSI dumps will be downloaded. False --dex / -dx DEX dumps will be downloaded. False

items.title: Parameters
items.text: Option Description Default --rules / -r The path to the folder with the rules, a platform alias (windows, linux) or an archive with already compiled rules. None --out / -o The path where the analysis results will be saved. ./sandbox --local / -l Compile rules locally using Docker (unix only). False --upload-timeout / -T This option allows you to increase the file upload timeout. For example, if you are uploading a large file with a slow internet. 300 in seconds --wait-timeout / -W Task waiting time in seconds (useful for heavy samples). None --unpack / -U The downloaded logs will be automatically converted. Learn more in Analyzing logs. False --decompress / -D Since process dumps are downloaded in a compressed format, this option allows them to be decompressed automatically. False --open-browser / -ob Open the analysis link in the default browser. False --preserve-filename / -pf Do not change filename for analysis. By default the path is flattened to sandbox/guest/os/filename. False

items.title: Sandbox Options
items.text:
Option Description Default --image / -i The image on which the behavioral analysis will be performed. None --key / -k The name of the key for accessing a specific sandbox. Repeat to spread the files over several sandboxes. None --name / -n The name of the file that will be in the sandbox. {filename} --timeout / -t Analysis duration. 300 in seconds --syscall-hooks / -s Read more about it in py-ptsandbox. None --dll-hooks-dir / -dll Read more about it in py-ptsandbox. None --unimon-hooks / -u Path to file with unimon hooks. None --fileextractor-excludes / -fe Path to file with fileextractor excludes. None --procdump-excludes / -pe Path to file with procdump excludes. None --unpack-archives / -ua Unpack archives with the config passwords and analyze every extracted file (not with -dc, -e, -S, -V). None --cmd Read more about it in py-ptsandbox. None --priority / -pr Read more about it in py-ptsandbox. 3 --no-procdumps-on-finish / -P Disable dumps for all created and not finished processes. False --disable-lightweight-dumps / -dl Disable lightweight memory dumps (mostly for testing purposes). False --bootkitmon / -b Read more about it in py-ptsandbox. False --bootkitmon-duration / -bd Read more about it in py-ptsandbox. 60 --mitm-disabled / -M Read more about it in py-ptsandbox. False --disable-clicker / -dc Read more about it in py-ptsandbox. False --skip-sample-run / -S Read more about it in py-ptsandbox. False --vnc-mode / -V Read more about it in py-ptsandbox. disabled --extra-files / -e Read more about it in py-ptsandbox. None --outbound-connections / -oc Whitelist of IP addresses to which connections from a VM are allowed (backconnect). None --file-type-as-ext / -fte Use a file type as an extension for a file. None

Tip

You can specify several images, for example:

sandbox-cli scanner scan-new -i win10-1803-x64 -i win11-23H2-x64

Tip

You can specify several extra files, for example:

sandbox-cli scanner scan-new -e file1 -e file2 -e file3 ...

items.title: Starting a manual analysis
items.text:
# -V full - a task will be created in a special mode with support for manual analysis
# -dc - disabling the clicker to control the mouse yourself
# -i - selecting a scan image
# -t 300 - behavioral analysis time (5 min)
$ sandbox-cli scanner scan-new -V full -dc -i ubuntu-jammy-x64 -t 300 malware.elf

items.title: Scan a password-protected archive
items.text:
# -ua - unpack the archive with the passwords from the config
$ sandbox-cli scanner scan-new -ua -i windows -t 120 samples.zip

Each extracted file gets its own folder: sandbox/<image>/<file>/.

items.title: Scan the sample on all available windows images
items.text:
For example, there are only three Windows images available on the stand, and analysis will be launched on all of them.

$ sandbox-cli scanner scan-new -i windows -t 120 malware.elf

[INFO] Using key: name=test-1 max_workers=8
[INFO] Scanning on: win10-22H2-x64, win10-1803-x64, win11-23H2-x64

...

Tip

Change -i windows to -i linux if you need to scan on all available linux images.

items.title: Scanning a large amount of samples at a time
items.text:
# -U - automatic unpacking of logs
$ sandbox-cli scanner scan-new -U -i win11-23H2-x64 -t 120 samples/*.exe

items.title: Spreading samples over several sandboxes
items.text:
# every -k adds a sandbox from the config
$ sandbox-cli scanner scan-new -k main -k second -t 120 samples/

Every sandbox runs up to its max-workers tasks at a time and takes the next sample as soon as one of its tasks finishes, so a faster sandbox gets more samples. Samples are read from disk only when they are uploaded. Only the images every sandbox has are used, and the rules and hooks are uploaded to each of them. A sandbox that can't be reached is dropped and its samples go to the others. scan_config.json of every result keeps the key it ran on.

But in general, if you are interested in some of the images, then I think you can find out more information from the manager.

items.title: Scan
items.text:
Warning

This is an outdated option and not supported as well as others, it is recommended to use Advanced scan.

The documentation for the options can be viewed in the same section.

It still remains because the old versions of the sandbox don't support the new API.

items.title: Quick start
items.text: $ sandbox-cli scanner scan -t 120 malware
